key_insight: In Parkinson’s disease, biofluid protein profiles reflect both disease burden and medication effects, highlighting the need to distinguish neurodegenerative from therapeutic signals.
clinical_relevance: These findings could support more objective Parkinson’s disease monitoring and trial assessments, but do not establish a validated clinical test.
method: Developed quality-control measures for longitudinal, high-throughput plasma and cerebrospinal fluid proteomics.
Refined clinical progression metrics and linked proteins to disease burden, disease activity, and medication dosage.
Used pathway and tissue-expression analyses to interpret protein changes.
evidence_signal: Across 850 plasma and 1,200 cerebrospinal fluid biosamples from 832 participants, the study identified 68 plasma and 3 cerebrospinal fluid disease-burden biomarkers, 4 plasma disease-activity biomarkers, and medication-dose associations involving 96 plasma and 34 cerebrospinal fluid proteins.
watch_item: Medication-associated protein changes complicate disease monitoring; the abstract does not report independent clinical validation, and this is Parkinson’s proteomics research—not AI cancer drug discovery.
paper_title: Resolving neurodegenerative and therapeutic crosstalk in biofluid proteomes for Parkinson's disease surveillance
